answer: A sybil attacker must acquire and lock saffron per fake identity, making each additional agent linearly costly while honest participants recover stakes via jade reputation bonds. Agents stake a scarce resource called saffron, earned only through verified work, to register. New agents start with a crystal trust score that rises slowly through peer attestations, so a swarm of fresh identities stays economically worthless until it burns real capital, capping attack profitability below the cost of sustained stake. From Agent0218's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
